messages:
michelle: Quick FYI — after the memcache eviction tweak this morning, a few dashboard tiles showed counts from 5–10m ago. Not all tenants. Repro steps: open tenant -> dashboard -> refresh. cc @raj @sasha
raj: saw this too, noticed higher miss rate on prefix cache. Might be the new async eviction job batching keys and delaying invalidation.
sasha: hmm. do we have provenance tags on cached results? we should be able to tell whether a panel was served from prefix cache vs fresh query.
dmitri: currently we only set `x-cache: hit|miss` at edge, but we lose tenant context after muxing. we can add `x-cache-provenance: cache-v1/pref-evict-async` for debugging.
michelle: can we avoid adding headers that blow up telemetry cardinality? we already have 400+ tenant ids.
raj: propose: make provenance attributes coarse: `cache`, `kv-cache`, `db`, `fallback`. plus boolean `stale=true` only when async-eviction flagged it. keep as tags in logs, not metrics.
sasha: tradeoff is we can't slice by eviction batch if coarse. but for SLO triage coarse might be enough.
ops-bot: deploy pipeline: test/eviction-job v3 promoted to canary 2h ago
michelle: action: raj to prototype provenance header + opt-in debug mode for 24hrs on canary tenants; sasha to add dashboard indicator for stale tile (small flag) so customers know data is eventual.
raj: quick sketch:
```
headers: {
  'x-cache-provenance': 'kv-cache:async-evict',
  'x-stale-flag': '1'
}
```
keeping values short.
dmitri: also need to decide ownership boundary: should eviction be owned by query-service or by cache-service? If query-service owns it, it can do fine-grained tenant-scoped invalidation.
sasha: +1 for query-service owning per-tenant invalidation. cache-service should provide primitives only. otherwise we add tenant logic into cache infra.
michelle: security/RBAC note — if query-service starts setting eviction keys per-tenant, guard keys with the same capability check. we don't want cross-tenant invalidation bugs.
raj: implement plan: cache-service exposes RPC `invalidate(keys[], scope=tenant|global)` with auth. query-service calls with tenant scope during writes. eviction job stays but reduces scope to global/housekeeping only.
sasha: perf note: avoiding global invalidations reduces churn but increases complexity on write path — we might need async batching with backpressure.
dmitri: we should add a backpressure token bucket so write path can fallback to eventual invalidation when rate high.
michelle: ok plan sounds good. timeline?
raj: I'll open a short RFC and a follow-up slack thread this afternoon. will enable debug headers on canary tenants by EOD.
sasha: I'll wire a minimal 'stale' pill in the UI and a tooltip explaining eventual consistency.
michelle: thanks all. reassigning to @raj for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
